scope.flow: redelegateWithdrawnHYPE re-delegation of cancelled withdrawal amounts via _distributeStake SpotDeposit

statements.text: A user cancels a withdrawal request via cancelWithdrawal, recording the associated HYPE value (totalHypeValueReturned) in _cancelledWithdrawalAmount.
The caller of redelegateWithdrawnHYPE holds MANAGER_ROLE privileges.
The _cancelledWithdrawalAmount value has a nonzero remainder modulo 1e10 wei HYPE.
The MANAGER_ROLE account calls redelegateWithdrawnHYPE, which reads _cancelledWithdrawalAmount and resets it to zero.
The amount is re-delegated through _distributeStake with operation type OperationType.SpotDeposit.
_distributeStake calls _convertTo8Decimals(amount, false), computing truncatedAmount = amount / 1e10 with roundUp false.

Unlike UserDeposit handling, the SpotDeposit/RebalanceDeposit conversion does not account for the amount % 1e10 remainder, which is neither added back to hypeBuffer nor included in truncatedAmount sent to L1.
Each redelegateWithdrawnHYPE call loses _cancelledWithdrawalAmount % 1e10 HYPE from the re-delegation process, which remains in the StakingManager contract outside normal accounting.
The stranded HYPE is neither recorded in totalStaked, explicitly tracked in hypeBuffer, nor delegated to validators to generate rewards.
As cancel-and-redelegate operations accumulate, the lost HYPE grows and becomes permanently stranded, unusable by the protocol or returnable to users.
The stranded value reduces protocol capital efficiency and directly diminishes potential profits for all kHYPE holders.
Re-delegating cancelled withdrawal amounts should account for the amount % 1e10 remainder so no HYPE falls outside hypeBuffer, totalStaked, or L1 delegation.
The truncated remainder is less than 1e10 wei HYPE (less than 1e-8 HYPE).

ambiguities: Report does not state whether a nonzero remainder scenario was actually observed; it is a conditional possibility.
Exact location of stranded HYPE (contract ETH balance vs L1 account) is described as implementation-dependent.
No explicit statement that the caller is unauthorized; MANAGER_ROLE is required.
